paper.title: Neural activity profiles reveal overlapping, intermingled subpopulations spanning area borders in mouse sensorimotor cortex

nodes.text: How are the activity patterns of individual cortical cells organized across sensorimotor cortex during behavior, and how does this relate to anatomical mapping?
nodes.description: The central question posed in the Introduction, framing whether neural response categories align with anatomical area boundaries or span them in overlapping spatial footprints.
nodes.anchor: how are the activity patterns of individual cortical cells organized across sensorimotor cortex during behavior, and how does this relate to previous anatomical mapping?

nodes.text: Do neurons form distinct categories spatially aligned to anatomical boundaries, or do categories span area boundaries in overlapping or abutting spatial footprints?
nodes.description: A more specific formulation of the organizational question, contrasting discrete area-aligned clusters versus distributed, overlapping subpopulations.
nodes.anchor: Cells could form distinct 'categories' or clusters that are spatially well-aligned to the boundaries of anatomically defined regions. Or, categories of neurons might span area boundaries in spatial footprints that do not relate obviously to area boundaries

nodes.text: Neuronal response profiles shift abruptly at anatomical borders between sensorimotor areas.
nodes.description: Motor areas show sharper tuning and more linear target-location relationships; somatosensory areas show more heterogeneous response patterns. This is a main conclusion from the PETH feature gradient analysis.
nodes.anchor: Neuronal response profiles often shifted abruptly at anatomical borders: motor areas showed sharper tuning and more linear relationships with target location, whereas somatosensory areas displayed more heterogeneous response patterns.

nodes.text: Neural response properties differ according to somatotopic representation, not only by anatomical area.
nodes.description: Properties such as tuning sharpness, response duration, and linearity of responses with respect to target location vary with somatotopy (forelimb vs hindlimb vs trunk representations).
nodes.anchor: Neural response properties also differed according to somatotopic representation.

nodes.text: Areas vary in their average response profiles but do not have well-separated feature distributions; instead, each area contains multiple subpopulations.
nodes.description: t-SNE of PETH features shows overlapping distributions across areas with multimodal within-area structure, indicating subpopulations rather than area-homogeneous populations.
nodes.anchor: areas varied in their average response profiles, but that areas did not have well-separated feature distributions; instead, each area contained subpopulations.

nodes.text: Four distinct subpopulations with characteristic response profiles span multiple cortical areas and spatially overlap with salt-and-pepper intermingling.
nodes.description: The Anterior, Forelimb motor, Forelimb somatomotor, and Hindlimb somatomotor subpopulations were identified by clustering GMM components across areas. Their members are intermingled in overlap zones and show similar response profiles across areas.
nodes.anchor: Together, these results describe novel activity structure across sensorimotor cortex and identify several distinct but spatially overlapping subpopulations with characteristic activity patterns during reach-to-grasp behavior.

nodes.text: The Anterior subpopulation is almost unique to M2 and shows high tuning persistence, sharp tuning, and highly linear target tuning.
nodes.description: Characterized as having a relatively abstract or external target representation.
nodes.anchor: One subpopulation, which we refer to as the 'Anterior' subpopulation, was almost unique to M2. It had uniquely high tuning persistence and tuning sharpness along with highly linear target tuning, arguing for a relatively abstract and external target repres

nodes.text: The Forelimb motor subpopulation spans M2 and the forelimb portion of M1, with strongly linear target tuning but less sharp and less persistent tuning than the Anterior subpopulation.
nodes.description: Its spatial footprint resembles the Medial Anterior Cortex (MAC) defined by corticofugal projection patterns.
nodes.anchor: A second subpopulation, the 'Forelimb motor' subpopulation, spanned M2 and the forelimb portion of M1. These neurons were also strongly linear in their target tuning, but less sharply tuned and with tuning that was somewhat less persistent.

nodes.text: The Forelimb somatomotor subpopulation spans M1 forelimb/orofacial zones and anterior S1-fl, with broad tuning, low linearity, low persistence, and brief responses.
nodes.description: Neurons in this subpopulation respond at characteristic times in the movement (low peak time variation).
nodes.anchor: The 'Forelimb somatomotor' subpopulation spanned M1 forelimb and orofacial zones and the anterior portion of S1-fl. This subpopulation was more broadly tuned, was less linearly tuned to target location, changed tuning over the course of the movement (low t

nodes.text: The Hindlimb somatomotor subpopulation is centered on S1-hl and spills into S1-tr, posterior S1-fl, and posterior M1/M2, with high peak time variability.
nodes.description: Similar to Forelimb somatomotor but neurons fire at different times for different targets.
nodes.anchor: Finally, a 'Hindlimb somatomotor' subpopulation was centered on S1-hl and spilled into S1-tr, the posterior portion of S1-fl, and the posterior tips of M1 and M2. This subpopulation was similar to the Forelimb somatomotor subpopulation, but each neuron no

nodes.text: Subpopulation members are locally salt-and-pepper intermingled in overlap zones, and PETH features within each subpopulation are similar across cortical areas.
nodes.description: Validated by classifying neurons to maximum-likelihood subpopulation and comparing likelihood map contours from area-specific GMM components.
nodes.anchor: members of the different subpopulations were locally salt-and-pepper intermingled, including in overlap zones. Subpopulations had nearly identical spatial footprints no matter which area was used to identify them.

nodes.text: 39,398 layer 2/3 neurons were recorded across 98 two-photon imaging sessions in six mice spanning M2, M1, S1-fl, S1-hl, and S1-tr.
nodes.description: Dataset scale and coverage.
nodes.anchor: A total of 39,398 neurons were extracted across the five relevant regions in the sensorimotor cortex. Dense sampling of layer 2/3 neurons was achieved using two-photon calcium imaging across 98 fields of view (FOVs) spanning the forelimb, hindlimb, and tru

nodes.text: Modulation fractions differed by area: M2 14%, M1 23%, S1-fl 30%, S1-hl 25%, S1-tr 27% (p<10^-16, chi-squared test).
nodes.description: Fraction of task-modulated neurons per area, cue-aligned.
nodes.anchor: The five areas of interest varied in the fraction of neurons that were modulated: M2 had 14%, M1 had 23%, S1-fl had 30%, S1-hl had 25%, and S1-tr had 27% (p<10 –16, Chi squared test for homogeneity).

nodes.text: Probability of modulation was highest at the M1/S1-fl border and lowest along the M1/M2 border.
nodes.description: Spatial map of modulation probability reveals sub-area structure.
nodes.anchor: The probability of a neuron being task-modulated was highest around the border between M1 and S1-fl, corresponding to the center of the forelimb portion of M1 and the proprioceptive region of S1-fl. Probability of modulation was particularly low in a wide

nodes.text: Response duration (autocorrelation FWHM) was highest in posterior regions (S1-tr, S1-hl, hindlimb M1/M2) and lowest in S1-fl and forelimb M1.
nodes.description: Measured as mean FWHM of autocorrelation across modulated targets per neuron.
nodes.anchor: This metric was highest in the posterior regions S1-tr, S1-hl, and the portions of M1 and M2 corresponding to the hindlimb.

nodes.text: Peak time variation (SD of peak times across targets) was low in M1 and high in posteromedial M2 and posterior S1-hl.
nodes.description: Correlated with signal-to-noise ratio (Spearman ρ = -0.53).
nodes.anchor: This metric was quite low in M1, indicating highly consistent timing of the activity peak (and reliable responses), and was highest in the posteromedial part of M2 (presumably corresponding to the hindlimb representation) and the posterior tip of S1-hl.

nodes.text: Tuning sharpness (1 - mean peak response/max peak response) was higher in forelimb-related subregions, with M2 neurons particularly sharply tuned.
nodes.description: Values near 1 indicate selectivity for few targets; near 0 indicate broad tuning.
nodes.anchor: This metric showed that neurons in forelimb-related subregions had sharper tuning than neurons in hindlimb-related regions, with M2 neurons being particularly sharply tuned.

nodes.text: Target tuning linearity (R^2 of peak response vs ordinal target distance from preferred target) was higher in motor areas (M2 > M1) than in somatosensory areas.
nodes.description: Measured as maximum R^2 across 15 anchor targets.
nodes.anchor: The resultant metric map shows that the motor areas were much more linearly tuned with respect to target location than were the somatosensory areas, with M2 even more linear than M1.

nodes.text: Tuning persistence (AUC of tuning-distance correlation curve) was highest in anterior M2, moderate in M1, and low in sensory regions.
nodes.description: Measures consistency of tuning profile across time relative to peak response.
nodes.anchor: Tuning persistence was highest in the anterior of M2, was moderate in M1, and was low in the sensory regions.

nodes.text: t-SNE of 5D PETH features showed neurons from each area distributed across most of the embedding space, with area-specific density peaks at different locations but overlapping distributions (all pairwise p<0.005, 2D KS test).
nodes.description: Demonstrates within-area diversity and between-area differences in feature distributions.
nodes.anchor: single neurons from each region were found across most of the t-SNE space. This makes clear that much of the diversity of neuron activity patterns was observed in each area. Second, when looking at where neurons in each area most commonly appeared in the t

nodes.text: GMM fits per area: M2 (4 components), M1 (3), S1-fl (2), S1-hl (1), S1-tr (1) by ICL criterion.
nodes.description: Number of mixture components selected for each area's PETH feature distribution.
nodes.anchor: M1, M2, and S1-fl were best modeled by the GMM as having multiple components: four for M2, three for M1, and two for S1-fl, while S1-hl and S1-tr were best modeled as being unimodal.

nodes.text: Bhattacharyya distances between GMM components across areas revealed four clusters of similar components, defining four subpopulations.
nodes.description: Hierarchical clustering of pairwise distances grouped components into Anterior, Forelimb motor, Forelimb somatomotor, Hindlimb somatomotor clusters.
nodes.anchor: This analysis revealed that many components identified independently in different areas were indeed highly similar and formed four clusters. We therefore combined components within each of the four clusters and took the neurons belonging to each cluster as

nodes.text: Subpopulation likelihood maps show overlapping spatial footprints: Anterior and Forelimb motor overlap in M2; Forelimb motor and Forelimb somatomotor overlap in forelimb M1; Forelimb somatomotor and Hindlimb somatomotor overlap at S1-fl/S1-hl border.
nodes.description: Gradient maps of subpopulation likelihoods match PETH feature gradient boundaries.
nodes.anchor: Notably, the high-likelihood regions for different subpopulations spatially overlapped. The Anterior and Forelimb motor subpopulations overlapped throughout M2; the Forelimb motor and the Forelimb somatomotor subpopulations overlapped in the forelimb porti

nodes.text: Classifying neurons to maximum-likelihood subpopulation confirmed salt-and-pepper intermingling and prevalence matching likelihood maps.
nodes.description: Spatial distribution of subpopulation memberships matches likelihood structure, indicating prevalence variation not response heterogeneity.
nodes.anchor: As expected, members of the different subpopulations were locally salt-and-pepper intermingled, including in overlap zones. Critically, we found that the prevalence of subpopulation membership across cortex matched the likelihood maps, implying that the sp

nodes.text: Likelihood map contours at 60% level for each subpopulation identified from different areas showed nearly identical spatial footprints.
nodes.description: Validates that subpopulation response profiles are homogeneous across areas.
nodes.anchor: Subpopulations had nearly identical spatial footprints no matter which area was used to identify them. This was true even in cases where only a small fraction of neurons in an area were members of that subpopulation.

nodes.text: Area-agnostic GMM on all neurons yielded three components matching three of four subpopulations (Anterior lost due to lower membership); median Adjusted Rand Index 0.856 across 50/50 splits.
nodes.description: Clustering reliability and validation.

nodes.text: Dense two-photon calcium imaging of layer 2/3 neurons across five sensorimotor areas (M2, M1, S1-fl, S1-hl, S1-tr) in six head-fixed mice performing a 15-target reach-to-grasp-to-drink task.
nodes.description: 98 fields of view, 39,398 neurons, GCaMP8s expression in Slc17a7-Cre mice, aligned to Allen CCF v3 via widefield vasculature and paw vibration mapping.

nodes.text: ZETA modulation test: trial-averaged responses compared to circularly permuted trial-averages per target, modulation score = max difference between real and shuffled data, p≤0.01 for any target considered modulated, computed separately for cue (-200 to +400 ms), lift (-200 to +400 ms), and contact (-300 to +300 ms) alignments.
nodes.description: Statistical test for task-related modulation.

nodes.text: PETH feature computations: response duration (mean autocorrelation FWHM across modulated targets), peak time variation (SD of peak times across targets with peak ≥25% of max), tuning sharpness (1 - mean peak/max peak across 14 non-preferred targets), target tuning linearity (max R^2 of peak response vs ordinal target distance across 15 anchor targets), tuning persistence (AUC of Pearson correlation between instantaneous tuning vector and anchor tuning vector at peak response time), local dimensionality (participation ratio of 30 nearest neighbors' PETH covariance eigenvalues).
nodes.description: Five interpretable PETH features plus local dimensionality metric.

nodes.description: Visualization of population feature space structure.
nodes.anchor: We used t-SNE to visualize the structure of our neural population's feature space. Each neuron was represented by a five-dimensional feature vector comprising the PETH feature values described above. To improve the representation of large-scale structure,

nodes.description: Probabilistic modeling of feature distributions and cross-area component comparison.

nodes.description: Quantification of spatial feature transitions and validation via decoding.

nodes.text: Relate the identified subpopulations to specific movement kinematics, target location, sensory feedback, and other behavioral variables to determine their functional roles.
nodes.description: Future work needed to link subpopulation activity patterns to behavior.
nodes.anchor: determining the relationships of the observed activity patterns to function will require specific attempts to link the activity to kinematics, target location, sensory feedback, and more; these relationships will be addressed in future work.

nodes.text: Record projection neurons between areas and from other layers to distinguish whether subpopulations reflect distributed recurrent circuits or broadcast activity from a single area.
nodes.description: Critical test of circuit hypotheses for area-spanning subpopulations.
nodes.anchor: Recording neurons that project from one area to another, and recording from other layers corresponding to later stages of processing and outputs, will be critical to distinguishing these hypotheses and more fully understanding these circuits.

nodes.text: Analyze single-trial dynamics and noise correlations within and across subpopulations using simultaneous multi-area recordings.
nodes.description: Current work used trial-averaged responses only.
nodes.anchor: Future work could leverage simultaneous recording of multiple areas to investigate single-trial co-fluctuations in neural activity within subpopulations and across areas.

nodes.text: Test whether the identified subpopulations exist in human sensorimotor cortex and elucidate their contributions to movement control.
nodes.description: Translational future direction mentioned in eLife digest.
nodes.anchor: However, realizing such benefits would first require confirming that these subpopulations exist in the human brain and elucidating their contributions to movement control.
